opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — shown net of a $10M licensing gain.

footerNote: Cost of sales of $2,971M includes $231M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, on top of $2,740M of cost of sales before that amortization, following AMD's own presentation of its income statement. The amortization line in operating expenses is shown as $362M — AMD's $372M of amortization net of a $10M licensing gain. The tax line was a $41M provision.
otherDetail: Other income of $55M, plus $7M of equity income from an investee, less $25M of interest expense — a net +$37M.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — revenue hit a record $2.8B, up 115%, driven by the steep ramp of Instinct GPU shipments and strong growth in 4th Gen EPYC CPU sales.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — up 49% primarily driven by sales of AMD Ryzen processors.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — down 59% primarily due to a decrease in semi-custom revenue.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into industrial, communications and other equipment (the Xilinx business) — down 41% as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit a record $2.8B, up 115% YoY, on the steep ramp of Instinct AI GPUs and strong 4th Gen EPYC sales — it is now nearly half of everything AMD sells.
takeaways.title: Data Center more than doubled

takeaways.text: Gross margin reached 49%, up from 46% a year ago — operating income swung to $269M from a $20M loss a year ago and net income reached $265M, up from $27M.
takeaways.title: Margins and profit recovered

takeaways.text: Gaming revenue fell 59% to $648M on lower semi-custom console revenue and Embedded fell 41% to $861M as customers normalized inventories — together they masked how fast the AI-driven businesses are growing.
takeaways.title: Gaming and Embedded still shrinking

verdict: AMD's revenue rose 9% to $5.8B as Data Center sales more than doubled to a record $2.8B on AI demand, lifting net income to $265M even as Gaming and Embedded revenue fell sharply.
